0.name: cvt_get_clock_slot
0.docs:
Returns the slot most recently produced by [`cvt_get_next_clock_slot`].

Asserts (`cvlr_assert!`) that [`cvt_get_next_clock_slot`] has been called
before in the rule; otherwise the rule fails at this call.

151.name: spl_close_account
151.docs:
Summary for SPL Token close_account instruction

Returns `Err(ProgramError::InvalidAccountData)` if `src_info` and
`dst_info` have **different** keys, or if the source's token amount is
non-zero; otherwise returns `Ok(())`. It changes no account: lamports are
not moved to the destination and the source is not closed or cleared.

Note that the key check is the reverse of the Token program's, which
rejects a close whose source and destination are the *same* account. As
written, this model succeeds only for self-closes, so a rule that closes a
token account into a different destination sees an error.

12.name: clog_acc_info
12.docs:
Logs an account to the counterexample call trace, tagged with the source
text of the argument.

`clog_acc_info!(acc)` is
[`cvlr_clog_account_info`](crate::cvlr_clog_account_info)`(stringify!(acc),
acc)`; `acc` must be a `&AccountInfo`.

150.name: spl_burn
150.docs:
Summary for SPL Token Burn instruction

Assumes the source holds at least `amount` (executions where it does not
are dropped), then subtracts `amount` from the source's token amount and
from the mint's supply, panicking if the supply would underflow. Always
returns `Ok(())`. Note the argument order: mint first, then the token
account. `_authority` is ignored.

11.name: Pk
11.docs:
A lightweight wrapper around a borrowed [`Pubkey`] that provides
convenience methods and logging capabilities.

`Pubkey` does not implement `CvlrLog`; wrap it to log it:
`clog!(Pk(acc.key) => "vault key")`. The key is shown as a 256-bit integer
(its 32 bytes read as a little-endian number), so two logged keys can be
compared at a glance. `Pk` dereferences to `Pubkey` and converts from and
to `&Pubkey`.

162.name: impl_nondet_mint
162.docs:
Defines a function returning an arbitrary SPL mint.

`impl_nondet_mint!(name, MintType)` defines `pub fn name() -> MintType`,
which builds a `MintType` with an arbitrary `supply`, `decimals` and
`is_initialized`, and `mint_authority` and `freeze_authority` that are
each arbitrarily `None` or an arbitrary key. `MintType` must be a path to a
struct with exactly those five fields, such as `spl_token::state::Mint` or
`spl_token_2022::state::Mint`, and the calling crate must depend on
`cvlr_nondet` (the expansion names it directly):

```ignore
cvlr_solana::impl_nondet_mint!(nondet_token_mint, spl_token::state::Mint);
```

149.name: spl_mint_to
149.docs:
Summary for SPL Token MintTo instruction

Adds `amount` to the mint's supply and to the destination's token amount,
panicking if either would overflow. Always returns `Ok(())`. `_authority`
is ignored, and `dst_info` is not checked to belong to the mint.

161.name: invoke_signed
161.docs:
Program-side replacement for `solana_program::program::invoke_signed`.

`invoke_signed!(instruction, account_infos, signer_seeds)` expands to
`solana_program::program::invoke_signed_unchecked(instruction, account_infos, signer_seeds)`.
As with [`invoke!`](crate::invoke), the called program is **not modeled**:
the call returns an arbitrary result and changes no account under the
standard summaries, and the Prover's CPI substitution does not apply.

148.name: spl_token_2022_transfer
148.docs:
Summary for SPL Token 2022 transfer instruction
This summary ignores extensions from SPL Token 2022 (e.g., fees)

Identical to [`spl_token_transfer`]; in particular no transfer fee is
withheld.

22.name: cvlr_nondet_coption
22.docs:
Either `COption::None` or `COption::Some(func())`, chosen arbitrarily.

The `COption` counterpart of `cvlr::nondet::nondet_option`, for the
optional fields of SPL Token state (e.g. a mint's authorities or an
account's delegate). `func` is called only on the `Some` path.

9.name: cvlr_new_account_info
9.docs:
Returns one `AccountInfo` with arbitrary contents, laid out as the Solana
runtime lays out program inputs.

Each call reserves a fresh, fixed memory region for the account (the Prover
gives every call its own 10 MiB range in the SVM input region), so the
`key`, `owner`, `lamports` and `data` of different accounts never share
memory. Their *values* are unconstrained:

* `key` and `owner` are arbitrary. In particular, two accounts may have the
  same key; assume `a.key != b.key` where the program relies on distinct
  accounts.
* `is_signer`, `is_writable` and `executable` are arbitrary.
* `lamports` and `rent_epoch` are arbitrary `u64`s.
* `data` has an arbitrary length of at most 8 MiB and arbitrary contents,
  with room after it for the runtime's permitted realloc increase
  (`MAX_PERMITTED_DATA_INCREASE`); the recorded original data length equals
  the length.

Constrain the account with `cvlr_assume!` (e.g. on its owner, data length
or deserialized contents) to match what the program expects. Usually called
through [`cvlr_deserialize_nondet_accounts`].

160.name: invoke
160.docs:
Program-side replacement for `solana_program::program::invoke`.

`invoke!(instruction, account_infos)` expands to
`solana_program::program::invoke_signed_unchecked(instruction, account_infos, &[])`,
which skips the runtime's signer and privilege checks. Use it in the code
under verification (typically behind the verification feature) in place of
`invoke(...)`; the calling crate must depend on `solana_program`.

**This macro does not model the called program.** The standard Prover
summaries (`cvlr_summaries_core.txt` in Certora's Solana template) treat
`invoke_signed_unchecked` as returning an arbitrary result, `Ok` or an
error, with no effect on any account. The callee's effects, such as a token
transfer, are not represented. Because the call no longer goes through
`invoke`, the Prover's CPI substitution (see the `cvlr-spl-token` crate)
does not apply to it either. To model a callee, call a model of it
directly (e.g. `cvlr_solana::token::spl_token_transfer`) or mock the
wrapper function with `#[cvlr::mock_fn]`.

109.name: new
109.docs: Creates a new owned wrapper from a [`Pubkey`].

159.name: require_keys_neq
159.docs:
Verification replacement for Anchor's `require_keys_neq!`: *assumes* the
two keys differ.

`require_keys_neq!(a, b)` and `require_keys_neq!(a, b, error_code)` expand
to `cvt::CVT_assume(a != b)`; the error code is ignored. See
[`require_keys_eq!`](crate::require_keys_eq) for the consequences and for
the `cvt::CVT_assume` the calling crate must provide.

146.name: spl_token_transfer
146.docs:
Summary for SPL Token transfer instruction

If `src_info` and `dst_info` have different keys, assumes the source
holds at least `amount` (executions where it does not are dropped), moves
`amount` from the source's to the destination's token amount, and panics
if the destination amount would overflow. If the keys are equal, nothing
changes. Always returns `Ok(())`. `authority_info` is ignored, and neither
account's mint or owner is checked.

7.name: fun_acc_infos_with_mem_layout

158.name: require_keys_eq
158.docs:
Verification replacement for Anchor's `require_keys_eq!`: *assumes* the two
keys are equal.

`require_keys_eq!(a, b)` and `require_keys_eq!(a, b, error_code)` expand to
`cvt::CVT_assume(a == b)`; the error code is ignored. Where Anchor's macro
returns an error when the keys differ, this one drops those executions
from the analysis, so rules only consider executions in which the check
passes.

The expansion names `cvt::CVT_assume`, a function of the legacy `cvt`
crate, so the calling crate must have `cvt::CVT_assume(bool)` in scope. A
shim is enough:

```ignore
mod cvt {
    pub use cvlr::asserts::cvlr_assume_checked as CVT_assume;
}
```

Unpack only decimals from `mint` base

18.name: cvlr_nondet_pubkey
18.docs:
An arbitrary `Pubkey`.

Every call returns an independent value, which may equal any other key.
The Prover models the underlying `CVT_nondet_pubkey` builtin through the
project's summaries file (`cvlr_summaries_core.txt` in Certora's Solana
template), which makes all 32 bytes arbitrary. With the `rt` feature it
returns `Pubkey::default()`.

5.name: cvlr_nondet_account_info
5.docs:
Returns an `AccountInfo` produced by the `CVT_nondet_account_info` builtin.

Prefer [`cvlr_new_account_info`](crate::cvlr_new_account_info). The Prover
marks this builtin as deprecated: by default it treats the call as a
no-op, so the returned `AccountInfo`, including its pointer fields, is
whatever was in memory. It is modeled only when the Prover runs with
`-solanaCvtNondetAccountInfo true` and the project's summaries file
describes it (as `cvlr_summaries_core.txt` from Certora's Solana template
does).

143.name: spl_mint_get_supply
143.docs:
Unpack only supply from `mint` base

Returns the `supply` field of the mint account `mint`.

166.name: cvlr_solana
166.docs:
Solana support for CVLR, the Certora Verification Language for Rust.

Helpers for writing Certora Prover rules about Solana programs:

* **Accounts.** [`cvlr_deserialize_nondet_accounts`] returns 16
  arbitrary `AccountInfo`s, the usual input of a rule; pass them to the
  program's processor. [`cvlr_new_account_info`] creates one.
* **Nondeterministic values.** [`cvlr_nondet_pubkey`],
  [`cvlr_nondet_option_pubkey`], [`cvlr_nondet_coption`],
  [`cvlr_nondet_coption_pubkey`].
* **Logging.** [`cvlr_clog_account_info`] / [`clog_acc_info!`] show an
  account in the counterexample; [`pubkey::Pk`] makes a `Pubkey` loggable
  with `clog!`.
* **Models of the environment.** [`token`] reads and writes SPL Token
  account and mint fields and models Token instructions;
  [`cvt_get_next_clock_slot`] models the clock slot; [`invoke!`] and
  [`invoke_signed!`] replace CPIs; [`require_keys_eq!`] and
  [`require_keys_neq!`] replace Anchor's checks.

SPL Token CPI mocks are in the `cvlr-spl-token` crate and a model of the
Stake program is in `cvlr-solana-stake`.

Several functions here rely on the Prover summaries in
`cvlr_summaries_core.txt`, shipped with Certora's Solana project template;
those are noted where they apply.

140.name: pubkey
140.docs: Wrappers that make a [`Pubkey`] loggable with `clog!`.

1.name: cvt_get_next_clock_slot
1.docs:
Advances a modeled clock and returns the new slot.

Returns an arbitrary slot that is strictly greater than the one returned by
the previous call (the first call returns any slot), and records it for
[`cvt_get_clock_slot`]. Use these two functions in a mock of the program's
clock access (e.g. in place of `Clock::get()?.slot`) to model time moving
forward between operations within one rule. They are unrelated to the
`Clock` sysvar account; the state lives in a global variable for the
duration of the rule.

152.name: token
152.docs:
Summaries for Token and Token-2022

Field accessors for SPL Token accounts and mints, and models of Token
instructions that update those fields directly. The accessors read and
write the fixed-offset base layout (165 bytes for a token account, 82 for
a mint), which Token-2022 shares, and panic if the account's data is
shorter. Each borrows the account data mutably, so it panics if the data is
already borrowed.

The instruction models perform none of the Token program's checks
(ownership, authority and signer, mint match, frozen state, delegation) and
ignore Token-2022 extensions; they only move amounts. Arithmetic overflow
in a model panics, which ends that execution. `cvlr-spl-token` uses these
models as the Prover's CPI mocks.

13.name: cvlr_clog_account_info
13.docs:
Logs the main fields of an account to the counterexample call trace.

Emits `tag` as a message line, followed by the account's lamports, data
length, `is_signer` and `is_writable` (in that order, each under its own
label). The key, owner and data contents are not logged; log the key with
`clog!(Pk(acc.key))` (see [`Pk`](crate::pubkey::Pk)) if needed. As with
all logging, `tag` must be a string literal after inlining (the
[`clog_acc_info!`](crate::clog_acc_info) macro passes one).
